theme: मन, भक्ति, उपासना और प्रणाम | Mind, devotion, worship, and reverence
context: Krishna closes the chapter with instructions to Arjuna concerning mind, devotion, worship, bowing, and taking him as the supreme goal.
contextHindi: कृष्ण अध्याय का अंत मन, भक्ति, उपासना, प्रणाम और स्वयं को परम लक्ष्य मानने के निर्देशों से करते हैं।
sanskritDevanagari:
मन्मना भव मद्भक्तो मद्याजी मां नमस्कुरु |
मामेवैष्यसि युक्त्वैवमात्मानं मत्परायणः ||९-३४||
transliteration:
manmanā bhava madbhakto madyājī māṃ namaskuru .
māmevaiṣyasi yuktvaivamātmānaṃ matparāyaṇaḥ ||9-34||

wordByWord.meaning: mind fixed on Me; with Me as the center of thought
become; cultivate the state of being
My devotee; one devoted to Me
one who worships or sacrifices to Me
bow to Me; express humility and surrender
having thus united the self; integrating one’s whole being
dedicated to Me; focused on Me as the supreme goal
you shall come to Me; you will attain Me

spokenHindi: इस श्लोक में कृष्ण अर्जुन को भक्ति के कुछ सीधे अभ्यास बताते हैं। वे कहते हैं: “मुझमें मन लगाओ, मेरे भक्त बनो, मेरी पूजा करो और मुझे प्रणाम करो। इस तरह अपने आप को मुझसे जोड़कर, मुझे परम लक्ष्य मानते हुए, तुम मुझे प्राप्त करोगे।” “मन्मना भव” का अर्थ है कि मन कृष्ण में लगा रहे; इसका अर्थ कृष्ण का मन बन जाना नहीं है। “मद्भक्तः” यानी मेरा भक्त बनो। “मद्याजी” का अर्थ है मेरी पूजा या यज्ञ करो—यह अपने आप में हर कर्म को अर्पित करने का निर्देश नहीं है। कृष्ण यहाँ प्रणाम करने और उन्हें परम लक्ष्य मानने की बात भी कहते हैं। इन शब्दों को समझते हुए हम श्लोक के सीधे निर्देश और अपनी विस्तृत साधना के बीच फर्क रख सकते हैं। आधुनिक अभ्यास में इन निर्देशों में से एक को थोड़ी देर ध्यान से अपनाएँ। शरीर असुविधा में हो तो प्रणाम का सहज रूप चुनें। यह हमारी व्यावहारिक सावधानी है; श्रद्धा को शरीर पर जोर देने की परीक्षा न बनाएँ।
clearEnglish: Krishna closes the chapter with a direct set of instructions: keep the mind on him, be his devotee, worship him, and bow to him. Uniting the self in this way and taking him as the supreme goal, Arjuna will come to him. Each component belongs to the sentence; reducing it to thought alone would omit worship and reverence. Conversely, translating madyaji as an instruction to offer every possible action would merge this verse with another teaching. The supplied commentary reads the invitation as surrender of the whole being to the Lord without reservation. That is Sivananda's interpretive expansion and can be attributed as such. A modest present practice can choose a comfortable expression of remembrance or reverence rather than demand an immediate achievement of the entire ideal. Bowing may be adapted to physical needs, and devotional focus need not erase responsibility to others. These are our practical accommodations. The promised destination remains Krishna, keeping the passage's goal distinct from merely becoming more efficient or less distracted.

interpretationPerspectives.label: TEXT
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: The verse tells Arjuna to keep his mind fixed on Krishna, be His devotee, worship or sacrifice to Him, bow to Him, and take Him as the supreme goal. It does not say here to offer every action; that instruction appears explicitly in 9.27.

interpretationPerspectives.label: INFERENCE
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: The verse brings attention, devotion, worship, reverence, and the Lord as one's highest goal together. Offering all actions to the Lord can be a related practice, but it is not the wording of “मद्याजी” here; Krishna gives that instruction explicitly in 9.27.

interpretationPerspectives.label: COMMENTARY — Sri Swami Sivananda
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: Sivananda interprets the passage as surrender of the whole being to the Lord without reservation.

practicalApplication.label: A comfortable devotional pause
practicalApplication.text: Briefly remember Krishna and express reverence in a form comfortable for your body. Return to ordinary responsibilities with care.

reflectionQuestion: Which of the verse's devotional acts can I practice with attention today?
reflectionQuestionHindi: श्लोक के किस भक्ति कार्य को मैं आज ध्यान से कर सकता हूँ?
